from.place: Finite-field proof, finite modules: degree-two cyclic inflation for constant prime coefficients

title: Finite-field degree-two vanishing with constant prime coefficients
statement: Let K be a finite field, Ks a separable closure of K [def-pd-separable-closure], and ell a prime nonzero in K. Put G = Gal(Ks/K) with its Krull topology. The degree-two continuous cohomology H²(G, Z/ell), for the trivial discrete action and with cohomology as in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], vanishes. In the Lean presentation this is Ext² from the trivial integer module in the category of discrete abelian G-modules; the coefficient group is ULift of ZMod ell in universe u+1.

proof.text: By det-base-field-cd-galois-group, the absolute Galois group is the profinite completion of the integers, with finite cyclic quotients of all positive orders generated by Frobenius.

proof.text: Apply det-base-field-cd-cochains to the finite trivial module Z/ell. Continuous cochains factor through finite cyclic quotients, and their degree-two cohomology is the filtered colimit of quotient cohomology under inflation. Identify this with DiscreteModule.H using the proved source comparison DiscreteModule.hAddEquivContinuousCohomology.

proof.text: At a cyclic quotient of order n, refine to the quotient of order ell*n. The periodic-resolution inflation formula det-base-field-cd-inflation multiplies the degree-two map by ell, hence makes it zero because ell kills the coefficient module. Every class in the filtered colimit becomes zero. This also covers n=1. Thus the degree-two group is subsingleton.
